**Rahul Kumar Sablaniya**: Software Engineer 2 at Infoblox for 6 months with 4 years 10 months of total professional experience. Previous roles include Software Engineer 2 at Cisco, Software Engineer at NerdNerdy, and Software Development Summer Internship at NerdNerdy. Based in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India [IN].

---

Amazon sde2 interview experience
I recently completed my interview loop for the SDE2 role at Amazon, and I wanted to share my experience for anyone preparing for similar roles.

🔹 Round 1 — Problem Solving & Coding
Problem: Design an index for file search.
Each file had a path and some text content (lowercase letters).
I had to implement:
⭐ insert(filePath, text)
⭐ vector find(word)
⭐ vector findWithPrefix(prefix)
I used a hybrid approach with a Trie + HashSet for fast lookup and prefix search.
↖️ Response: Extremely positive.

🔹 Round 2 — Low Level Design (LLD)
Problem: Design a vehicle rental service (initially for 2-wheelers but extensible to 4-wheelers).
We discussed:
⭐ Database schemas, API design, Applying Factory and Strategy patterns
⭐ Handling concurrency issues: preventing double bookings, avoiding double payments, ensuring consistent inventory updates
↖️ Response: Extremely positive.

🔹 Round 3 — High Level Design (HLD), done by hiring manager
Problem: Design a notification service supporting push, email, and SMS.
Key discussions:
⭐ Handling different message priorities (e.g., OTP as real-time high-priority)
⭐ Using message queues, topics/partitions, retry and backoff strategies
↙️ Response: Negative.

🔹 Round 4 — Bar Raiser
⭐ This round focused entirely on Leadership Principles.
The interviewer skipped the coding/problem-solving part, and we had a 45-minute scenario-based discussion.
➡️ Response: Neutral.

Final verdict: Rejected
But the learning definitely does not stop here.
Growing every day and looking forward to more challenges ahead.

**Pawan Jindal**: SDE-2 at Amazon for 1 year 2 months with 6 years of total professional experience. Previous roles include Software Engineer 2 at Microsoft, SDE - 1 at Mobile Premier League (MPL), and Software Engineer at Paytm. Based in India [IN].

---

🧩 My [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE-2 Interview Experience —

A lot of people asked me about how the actual interview process went, so here is a clear breakdown of my [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE-2 interview journey.
Sharing this to help anyone preparing for [FAANG+](https://linkedin.com/company/faang-plus) or similar product-company roles. 🚀

1️⃣ Online Assessment (OA)
Content:
✔️ DSA questions
✔️ Behavioural section based on Leadership Principles
This was to evaluate both coding fundamentals and decision-making mindset.

2️⃣ Screening Round (DSA)
Focus: Priority Queue based problem
This round mainly tested depth of problem-solving, edge cases, and code quality.

3️⃣ Data Structures Round (DSA – Deep Dive)
Focus: Tree-based problem
Interviewer went into complexity analysis, optimization, and approach clarity.

4️⃣ Low-Level Design (LLD)
Task: Design a complete version of StackOverflow
Covered:
– Class design
– Data modeling
– Core flows (post, comment, vote, moderation)
– Extensibility & clean abstractions

5️⃣ High-Level Design (HLD)
Task: Design an Orchestrator Layer
They went deep into:
– System components
– Scaling concerns
– Async workflows
– Fault tolerance
– Trade-offs
Plus scenario-based Leadership Principle discussions.

6️⃣ Bar Raiser Round
Focus:
✔️ DSA
✔️ Leadership Principles
✔️ Past experience — ownership, impact, complex challenges
This round checked consistency, clarity, and long-term thinking.

🔔 Result: OFFER MIL GYA 🎉
Every round tested a different dimension — coding, design depth, ownership mindset, clarity of thought, and how you handle ambiguity.
If you’re preparing for similar roles, focus on:
🔹 Strong fundamentals
🔹 Structured thinking
🔹 Real ownership stories
🔹 Clear explanations and trade-offs
🔹 Calm mindset during hard follow-up questions

If you want me to break down:
✔️ how I prepared,
✔️ how I structured answers during interviews,
✔️ or how I explained my past work,
I’d be happy to help.

**Yasir Sharfi**: Software engineer II(L62) at Microsoft with 6 years 10 months of experience. Previous roles include Senior Software Engineer at Dell Technologies, Senior Software Engineer at Cisco, and Software Engineer at Bosch Global Software Technologies. Based in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India [IN].

---

🚀 Amazon SDE-2 Interview Experience

Interviewed for the Amazon SDE-2 role in April.
After clearing the OA, I was invited for 5 interview rounds (face-face).

Sharing a brief overview to help others preparing 👇
🧪 Round 1 – Data Structures & Algorithms
Design an efficient solution to find the top-K frequent elements from a large dataset.
Approach:
Used HashMap for frequency counting + Min Heap to keep top-K elements.
Time: `O(n log k)`, Space: `O(n)`.

🧪 Round 2 – Problem Solving (Graphs / Trees)
Find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) in a binary tree.
Approach:
Used DFS recursion, returning node when match found and bubbling results upward.
Focused on edge cases (null nodes, same inputs).

🧪 Round 3 – Low Level Design (LLD)
Design a parking lot system.
Approach:
Defined entities (`Vehicle`, `ParkingSlot`, `Ticket`), used OOP principles, enums, and basic extensibility.
Discussed scalability and edge cases.

🧪 Round 4 – High Level Design (HLD)
Design a URL Shortener.
Approach:
Covered APIs, database schema, hashing vs encoding, scalability, collision handling, and caching (Redis).

🧪 Round 5 – Behavioral (Leadership Principles)
Focus Areas:
* Ownership
* Bias for Action
* Handling conflicts
* Failure & learning

**Tip: STAR format is mandatory. Interviewer drilled deep into decisions and trade-offs.

### 📌 Final Verdict

After completing all rounds, the result was shared as “Not Hired”.
No specific feedback or reason was provided, which is standard for Amazon.

Grateful for the learning experience. Back to improving and moving forward 💪
